editorial.headline: The Travel Agency Code for Complex Journeys
editorial.standfirst: For medium and large travel agencies assembling complex itineraries, the national position is open to full foreign ownership—and Bali does not block PMA registration.
editorial.body:
KBLI 79129 covers travel-agency activity that sits outside the specifically enumerated travel-agency groupings. Its practical terrain is the assembled journey: arranging transport, accommodation, food, convention venues and travel documentation, whether the service is delivered online or offline. That can include passports, visas and equivalent documents, as well as the planning and packaging of the individual components that make a business trip work.

The code is particularly legible where travel has many moving parts and a clear professional purpose. The record gives the example of business-travel planning for athletes and sports teams competing at international events. The point is not merely booking a route or a room; it is coordinating the service elements around a trip so that transport, stays, meals, venues and documentation can be brought into one travel-agency operation.

Registration is open at the medium and large business scales. Nationally, the activity is marked open for PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, foreign ownership may reach the full national ceiling for this activity. That national position is sourced to the Presidential Regulations identified in the record, and it should be read alongside the scale limitation: this is an activity open to medium and large enterprises, not a catch-all invitation across every business scale.

Bali does not reverse that result. The province’s standing for this activity is recorded as OK or higher risk, and the Bali moratorium does not block PMA registration. The reason is specific: at the large scale, the OSS risk classification is medium-high or high. Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium applies to low and medium-low risk KBLI activities; this activity is therefore outside that block on the record provided. For a foreign founder considering a Bali-based travel-agency operation within this scope, the honest conclusion is straightforward: the activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali today.
